imageRegistry.description: Registry of every image, the controller-rendered airlock and tool server pods included; wins over each image's registry

imagePullSecrets.description: Pull Secret names for the chart's own pods (the controller-rendered pods run as the namespace's default ServiceAccount: give it the Secret, see README)

headless.description: Install without the AIsolate UI: the CRDs, the controller, default-deny, the aisolate Service and its routes, the egress proxy. false adds the AIsolate UI (frontend, backend, the backend's database). A bool, never a string

allowTags.description: Let tag-only images render, for clusters that build their own images; off, every AIsolate image needs its digest

extraDeploy.description: Extra objects to deploy with the release (rendered as templates)

toolServers.description: Tool server Services helm test must find unreachable (skipped while absent)

ingressService.description: The ingress controller's Service in the platform.egress.ingressFrom namespace, which helm test calls the release through

tag.description: helm test's curl image tag, used only with allowTags

digest.description: helm test's curl image digest (sha256:…), the chart's pin of 8.14.1; wins over the tag

pullPolicy.description: helm test's curl image pull policy

pullSecrets.description: helm test's curl image pull Secret names

tag.description: Controller image tag, used only with allowTags; empty: the chart's appVersion

digest.description: Controller image digest (sha256:…); required unless allowTags

resources.description: Controller container resources (requests, limits), e.g. for a namespace ResourceQuota

repository.description: Airlock image repository: the core of every airlock pod the controller renders

tag.description: Airlock image tag, used only with allowTags; empty: the chart's appVersion

digest.description: Airlock image digest (sha256:…); required unless allowTags

pullPolicy.description: Pull policy of every pod the controller renders, airlock and tool server alike

replicas.description: Replicas of every airlock pod, and of the discovery pods (the airlock image with no documents) behind the aisolate Service

runtimeClassName.description: RuntimeClass of every pod the controller renders (airlock, MCP server, discovery); empty: the cluster's default

corsAllowedOrigins.description: Browser origins the airlock pods answer, e.g. the chat's (with platform.chat.enabled, the origin of platform.chat.host)

resources.description: Requests and limits of every airlock pod and discovery pod (cpu, memory, ephemeral-storage, which holds the airlock's fetched code in /tmp, at most 2Gi): one airlock's code or load must not starve its node

repository.description: Tool server image repository: one pod per airlock, rendered by the controller

tag.description: Tool server image tag, used only with allowTags; empty: the chart's appVersion

digest.description: Tool server image digest (sha256:…); required unless allowTags

resources.description: Requests and limits of every MCP server (cpu, memory, ephemeral-storage, which holds the fetched code in /tmp, at most 2Gi)

repository.description: Python airlock image repository: the airlock pod of an airlock with Python code

tag.description: Python airlock image tag, used only with allowTags; empty: the chart's appVersion

digest.description: Python airlock image digest (sha256:…); required unless allowTags

repository.description: Python tool server image repository: the MCP server of an airlock with Python code

tag.description: Python tool server image tag, used only with allowTags; empty: the chart's appVersion

digest.description: Python tool server image digest (sha256:…); required unless allowTags

nodeSelector.description: Node labels every pod of the release must match: the chart's Deployments, the helm test and the pods the controller renders alike, e.g. {pool: aisolate} for a dedicated node pool

tolerations.description: Tolerations of every pod of the release, likewise: a dedicated pool's taint, e.g. [{key: pool, operator: Equal, value: aisolate, effect: NoSchedule}]

className.description: IngressClass of every Ingress, the chart's and the controller's

host.description: The release's public host: discovery and every airlock's endpoint

publicUrl.description: The release's public URL; its scheme serves the AIsolate UI's hosts too

tls.description: Serve every chart Ingress over TLS from the Secret named after it (aisolate-tls; with the AIsolate UI also ui-tls and backend-tls, with the chat chat-tls, with the chart's Keycloak keycloak-tls), provided by the installer or cert-manager; on ingress-nginx the release host's certificate covers the controller's Ingresses too

annotations.description: Annotations of every chart Ingress, over the chart's nginx ones, e.g. cert-manager.io/cluster-issuer

issuerUri.description: The application users' identity provider: the issuer the pods validate tokens against; the backend too unless operators.issuerUri is set; empty: the users realm of the chart's Keycloak (platform.keycloak.enabled), else required

jwkSetUri.description: Where the pods fetch the provider's keys; the backend too unless operators.issuerUri is set; empty with the chart's Keycloak: its in-cluster Service

rolesClaim.description: Dot path of the roles claim in the tokens: the AIsolate UI roles, and the roles the rules name (Entra ID app roles: roles; Okta: groups); the pods read it, the backend too unless operators.rolesClaim is set

egress.description: The provider as a NetworkPolicy peer, when it runs in the cluster or at a private address: namespaceSelector, podSelector, cidr (/8 or longer, never with selectors), port (required); empty: the chart's Keycloak when it answers, else the backend reaches it over HTTPS at a public address

issuerUri.description: AIsolate's own identity provider for the dashboard and the CLI; empty: the operators realm of the chart's Keycloak (platform.keycloak.enabled), else the one above

jwkSetUri.description: Where the backend fetches that provider's keys; empty: discovered from the operators' issuer; the one above is used only when the issuer is shared

rolesClaim.description: Dot path of the roles claim in that provider's tokens; empty: the one above

egress.description: That provider as a NetworkPolicy peer (same keys as platform.identity.egress); empty: the one above

dns.description: The cluster DNS as a peer (default: kube-dns in kube-system, port 53): namespaceSelector, podSelector, cidr (/8 or longer, never with selectors), port (required)

ingressFrom.description: The only pods that may reach an airlock pod (default: the ingress-nginx namespace): namespaceSelector, podSelector or cidr (/8 or longer, never with selectors)

cidr.description: The Kubernetes API server's address, the controller's and the backend's way to it, e.g. the kubernetes Endpoints' IP/32 (kubectl get endpoints kubernetes -n default); empty: any address on the ports, which the install's notes warn of (on Cilium an ipBlock does not match a node-hosted API server: leave it empty there)

ports.description: The API server's ports as the pods' traffic reaches it after the Service: 443 on most managed clusters, 6443 on kubeadm, k3s and OpenShift, 8443 on minikube

hosts.description: The hosts of every LLM and data source defined for all of AIsolate or by a space or an airlock, each with its NetworkPolicy peer: cidr (/8 or longer), or namespaceSelector and podSelector, never both, plus port (required); an airlock that resolves an unmapped host is Invalid, and a global entry with one is left out of every catalog; a host on platform.egress.proxy.domains needs no entry

domains.description: Hostnames the CONNECT-only egress proxy may reach on port 443: exact names, *.example.com for its subdomains, .example.com for the name and its subdomains; the proxy renders when non-empty

tag.description: Egress proxy image tag, used only with allowTags

digest.description: Egress proxy image digest (sha256:…), the chart's pin of the tag; wins over it

pullSecrets.description: Egress proxy image pull Secret names

otlpEndpoint.description: OTLP/HTTP base URL the airlock and tool server pods send their traces to, e.g. an OpenTelemetry Collector, http://otel-collector.monitoring.svc:4318 (the pods append /v1/traces); its host must be in platform.egress.hosts or proxied, or every space is Invalid; empty: no trace leaves the pods

queryUrl.description: The trace store's query API the backend reads, Jaeger's (http://jaeger.monitoring.svc:16686) or any store that answers GET /api/traces/{id} as Jaeger does; empty: the AIsolate UI has no Monitoring

egress.description: The trace store as the backend's NetworkPolicy peer, required with queryUrl: namespaceSelector and podSelector, or cidr, plus its query port

queryUrl.description: The Prometheus HTTP API the backend reads, e.g. http://prometheus.monitoring.svc:9090, or any store that answers /api/v1/query and /api/v1/query_range alike; its series need the space label; empty: no Metrics tab

egress.description: Prometheus as the backend's NetworkPolicy peer, required with queryUrl: namespaceSelector and podSelector, or cidr, plus its port

failClosed.description: While an airlock pod's on-disk buffer of lines the backend has not taken is full, it refuses new questions with 503 "audit unavailable"; false: it answers and the line is lost from the backend's trail (stdout keeps it)

stdout.description: Each audit line is also printed to the airlock pod's stdout, for a SIEM's log collector; headless keeps it on regardless

retentionMonths.description: Months of audit lines the backend keeps (84: seven years); its daily job drops each older month whole

existingSecret.description: An existing Secret holding the audit ingest key under the key key; set: the chart creates no audit-ingest Secret and hashes none into the pod checksums, recommended for a render without cluster access (Argo CD, helm template), where lookup cannot keep the generated key; empty: the chart generates and keeps one

An existing Secret holding the key the backend seals typed API keys and passwords with, under the key key (32+ characters); set: the chart creates no credentials-key Secret and hashes none into the backend's checksum, recommended for a render without cluster access (Argo CD, helm template); empty: the chart generates and keeps one

repository.description: AIsolate UI image repository; the image carries the backend's URL and the operators' identity provider from its build (NEXT_PUBLIC_AISOLATE_URL, NEXT_PUBLIC_OIDC_AUTHORITY)

tag.description: AIsolate UI image tag, used only with allowTags; empty: the chart's appVersion

digest.description: AIsolate UI image digest (sha256:…); required unless allowTags

pullSecrets.description: AIsolate UI image pull Secret names

enabled.description: Install the AIsolate chat, the sample client, on its own host, with or without the AIsolate UI

host.description: The chat's host; add its origin to platform.airlock.corsAllowedOrigins

repository.description: Chat image repository; the image carries the release's URL from its build (NEXT_PUBLIC_AISOLATE_URL, a build arg of its Dockerfile)

tag.description: Chat image tag, used only with allowTags; empty: the chart's appVersion

digest.description: Chat image digest (sha256:…); required unless allowTags

hostAliases.description: Host entries of the chat pod (ip, hostnames), for a release host and identity provider the cluster's DNS does not resolve, as in the minikube demo

enabled.description: Install a Keycloak of the chart's own, a demo and trial identity provider with the two realms AIsolate needs: platform.identity and platform.identity.operators then default to its realms; a production install names its own provider there instead

host.description: The chart's Keycloak host: the issuer the browsers, the UI, the CLI and the chat see

repository.description: Keycloak image repository, the stock image: it imports the chart's two realms at its first start

tag.description: Keycloak image tag, used only with allowTags

digest.description: Keycloak image digest (sha256:…), the chart's pin of 26.7.3; wins over the tag

name.description: The operators' realm: the AIsolate UI (client aisolate-ui) and the CLI (aisolate-cli) sign in there; its realm roles aisolate-admin and aisolate-auditor

loginTheme.description: The realm's login theme, one the image carries (aisolate-ui in the themed image); empty: Keycloak's own. Imported with the realm: an existing instance takes a new one through the admin console, or with a recreated claim

name.description: The application users' realm: the chat (client aisolate-chat, and any client it registers from platform.chat.host) signs its users in there; the roles the rules name are its realm roles

loginTheme.description: The realm's login theme, one the image carries (aisolate in the themed image); empty: Keycloak's own; imported with the realm like the operators'

demoUsers.description: Create the demo cast at the first start (operators realm: admin, developer, auditor; users realm: jane the CEO, john the employee, auditor, with those realm roles), each with their password from the Secret

existingSecret.description: A Secret you create with Keycloak's admin password under the key admin-password (the demo admin's too) and, with demoUsers, developer-password, auditor-password, jane-password and john-password; empty: the chart generates the Secret keycloak with those keys and keeps it with lookup (set one for a render without a cluster, see persistence.postgres.existingSecret)

size.description: The size of the PersistentVolumeClaim keycloak its file database keeps the realms, users and registered clients on; the realms are imported into an empty one only: delete it to import them again

storageClass.description: Its StorageClass; empty: the cluster's default

host.description: Backend host (headless=false): the AIsolate UI's API and the CLI's endpoint

tag.description: Backend image tag, used only with allowTags; empty: the chart's appVersion

digest.description: Backend image digest (sha256:…); required unless allowTags

maxArtifactSize.description: Largest project artifact (a jar or a Python zip) a deploy may bring, as Spring reads a size (500MB, 2GB); empty: no limit. The pods fetch it from the backend at start

repository.description: The backend's PostgreSQL image repository; its data lives on the PersistentVolumeClaim db (storage)

tag.description: The backend's PostgreSQL image tag, used only with allowTags

digest.description: The backend's PostgreSQL image digest (sha256:…), the chart's pin of postgres:18; wins over the tag

pullPolicy.description: The backend's PostgreSQL image pull policy

pullSecrets.description: The backend's PostgreSQL image pull Secret names

resources.description: The backend's PostgreSQL container resources (requests, limits)

existingSecret.description: A Secret you create with the database password under the key password; empty: the chart generates the Secret db and keeps it with lookup, which a render without a cluster (Argo CD, helm template | kubectl apply) cannot see, so every sync makes a new password the kept database refuses: set one there

size.description: The size of the PersistentVolumeClaim db the database keeps its data on (the spaces, the airlocks, the audit trail); helm uninstall deletes it

storageClass.description: Its StorageClass; empty: the cluster's default
